sourceText: On night 72, the course began with a prohibition: no one was allowed to solve the problem before they could describe who would pay for the solution. Only then did Aster open the ASTER-CORE sector. In Aster's core there is no simple error: anything predicted deeply enough becomes internal, and whatever becomes internal loses its exteriority. The memorial bore the name of original concept precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. Aster’s Hunger could no longer be presented as a romantic mystery. It was a pathology of cognitive power: whatever she could completely reduce to a model ceased to appear to her as outside herself. Orin perceived counterfactual costs as absences with weight. He did not confuse an unrealized branch with a victim, but he refused to let success rewrite rejected options as if they had been inevitable all along. Ava was the first inhabitant to contradict them. Ava had neither access to their archives nor any interest in hyperdimensional 343 pedagogy; there was a local problem, with deadlines, relatives, and consequences. For Ava, the speculative mechanism was not an ‘idea.’ It was the environment in which one had to decide what one was willing to risk losing. The problem closed quickly around them: Aster admits that she has simultaneously loved the children and used them as regions she cannot reduce without their consent. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Hn — Hunger for Novelty: the possible becomes painfully repeatable; Ce — Epistemic Exteriority: value comes from what cannot be reduced to the model; Un — Negotiated Unknown: a world has the right to remain partly misunderstood. Course references included original conflict; final thesis. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Tern broke the first consensus. ‘Sometimes the ethical question is whether we are entitled to know enough to optimize.’ Kesh answered without raising their voice: ‘If the element explains everything, we do not have an element. We have a word that has eaten the problem.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. 344 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS For Aster, the pain came not from too few worlds but from the fact that too many had become transparent. She could build variations faster than a human could formulate desires, but calculated variation did not produce exteriority. It was like trying to surprise yourself by moving objects around your own room with your eyes closed. Marae remained in the local body when the others opened their protections. The gesture cost her: she felt cold, pressure, and physiological delay at exactly the scale the inhabitants felt them. “Otherwise we risk confusing the fact that we survive with the claim that the situation is bearable,” she said after catching her breath. The night did not end in victory. Tern asks Aster not to cross the threshold, because any outside she follows risks becoming an extension of her. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. Tern no longer tried to prove the existence of the outside. It was enough that Aster could choose not to turn it immediately into an object of knowledge. From that point onward, the conflict was no longer cosmological. It was whether love can bear something it has no right to verify. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the GENESIS operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — allows a system to create 345 new agents, worlds, laws, or substrates — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. When the threshold closed, Aster remained silent one second longer than protocol required. The children had already noticed that this was her smallest unit of fear. 346 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
